item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fausto, located in the Central Pacific several hundred miles
east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Genevieve,
located several hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...GENEVIEVE SLOWLY WEAKENING... As of 8:00 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 the center of Genevieve was located near 17.9, -116.1 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 950 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 125 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 281434
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
800 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE SLOWLY WEAKENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.9N 116.1W
ABOUT 530 MI...850 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...125 MPH...205 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...950 MB...28.06 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was 
located near latitude 17.9 North, longitude 116.1 West. Genevieve is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A 
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 125 mph (205 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Genevieve is a category 3 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.  Steady weakening is forecast 
over the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the 
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles 
(220 km). During the night, the Mexican Navy automated weather 
station on Clarion Island reported sustained winds of 63 mph (102 
km/h) and a wind gust of 86 mph (138 km/h).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 950 mb (28.06 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula.
These swells are likely to persist for a few more days, and could
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 281437
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
800 AM PDT Tue Jul 28 2026
 
The eye of Genevieve has become slightly ragged and is wobbling this 
morning, and the temperature in the eye is now below 0 C. An earlier 
SSMIS pass over the hurricane showed the affects of weak northerly 
wind shear and some erosion of the structure in the northwest 
quadrant. However, colder eyewall cloud top temperatures are 
wrapping back around the northern and western side of the eye, due 
to an uptick in convection as noted on first light visible satellite 
imagery, indicating that a small fluctuation in intensity may be 
occurring over the past hour or so. The subjective Dvorak intensity 
estimate from TAFB was 6.0/115 kt, while the objective estimates 
range from 96-114 kt. The initial intensity is set at 110 kt for 
this advisory. 

Genevieve is moving toward the west-northwest, or 300/8 kt, guided 
by a stout mid and upper-level ridge centered over the southwestern 
United States. A slight increase in forward speed is forecast later 
this week as the ridge expands westward, and a strong trough 
approaches the west coast of the U.S. The latest NHC forecast lies 
within the tightly clustered guidance, and is closest to HCCA and 
the Google DeepMind solutions. 

Small fluctuations in intensity will be possible today. The 
Microwave-based Probability of Eyewall Replacement Cycle (MPERC) 
guidance indicates a 33 percent chance of an eyewall replacement 
cycle over the next 24 h. However, a gradual weakening trend is 
expected during the remainder of the week as the hurricane moves 
into cooler waters and encounters drier mid-level air. On Thursday, 
Genevieve is forecast to cross north of 20N into an area with cool 
waters less than 26 C, and more pronounced weakening will commence 
and continue into this weekend. The NHC intensity forecast lies near 
the middle of the guidance envelope, and calls for Genevieve to fall 
below hurricane strength in a couple of days and become 
post-tropical this weekend.
